title: Q2 2026 Private Upgrade Pathways & Rollout Playbook
creator: Leah Martinez
description:
Goal: create an operationally-safe, auditable playbook to perform major and minor upgrades for Private/VPC/on-prem customers with minimal disruption and a clear migration path. This ticket scopes the Q2 plan for: (1) schema for upgrade bundles and compatible model/runtime pairs; (2) automated canary and staged rollouts across Dedicated and Private fleets; (3) rollback procedures and customer communication templates; (4) evaluation criteria for opt-in vs forced upgrades and required SLAs for each option.

Context: enterprise customers running Private deployments have requested clearer upgrade SLAs and a repeatable process to accept or delay breaking changes (kernel/quantization/runtime). Current ad-hoc upgrades have resulted in two incidents last quarter (see ENG-19822) and inconsistent customer expectations.

Scope & Deliverables:
- Upgrade compatibility matrix (models, quantization profiles, runtime versions).
- Automated canary orchestration (Helm/air-gapped patterns) and test harness for canonical workloads.
- Customer-facing upgrade schedule and rollback SLA language for contracts.
- Runbook for on-call + SRE that covers detection, mitigation, and postmortem template.
- Telemetry plan: runbook-driven dashboards, percentage of traffic on new version, error delta, latency P95/P99.

Acceptance criteria:
- Compatibility matrix published and approved by Applied ML and Runtime teams.
- Canary automation validated in staging with two enterprise test tenants and <1% error regression on synthetic workloads.
- Rollback executes end-to-end within defined SLA in rehearsal.
- Communication templates and opt-in controls added to Console and docs.

Trade-offs & decisions made so far:
- Chosen staged-canary default cadence = 3 waves (internal, pilot customers, broad) to balance safety and momentum. This increases release time by ~24–48 hours compared to immediate rollout but reduces customer-facing incidents.
- Default policy will prefer soft opt-in for major runtime changes; auto-upgrade only for critical security patches. This requires Console UI changes (separate ticket).

Progress updates (03/05–03/14):
- 2026-03-05: Kickoff with Applied ML, Runtime, SRE, and Legal. Collected initial incident logs from ENG-19822.
- 2026-03-09: Runtime team proposed compatibility schema v0.1; tradeoffs discussed re: KV cache incompatibilities. Action: ENG to prototype migration shim (ENG-19822).
- 2026-03-11: Legal reviewed rollback SLA draft; requested explicit data-retention disclosure for on-prem reverts. Follow-up assigned to PM (Leah).
- 2026-03-13: Design shipped wireframes for Console opt-in controls and upgrade timeline. Design feedback: reduce cognitive load for admins; show estimated downtime per wave.
- 2026-03-14: Canary runbook PR opened (GH #452). SRE scheduled rehearsal with two pilot customers in week of 2026-04-06.

Open risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Some quantized models require re-quantization which can change outputs (quality regressions). Mitigation: build gated quality checks and tie regressions to automated alerts; create rollback triggers based on eval thresholds.
- Risk: Air-gapped customers may not be able to accept staged canaries. Mitigation: document manual patch process and provide on-prem installer bundles; coordinate with Solutions Engineering for customer handoffs.

Stakeholders: Product (Leah, Omar), Runtime (Marcus Chen), Applied ML (Dr. Priya Rao), SRE (Nora Blake), Legal (Samir Kapoor), Design (Ivy Nguyen), Solutions Eng (Hector Alvarez).

- By 2026-03-21: ENG to deliver compatibility schema v0.2 and prototype migration shim (owner: Marcus Chen).
- By 2026-03-28: Design to finalize Console opt-in mocks and handoff to Frontend (owner: Ivy Nguyen).
- By 2026-04-06: SRE to run first rehearsal with pilot tenants; capture metrics and post-rehearsal notes (owner: Nora Blake).
